differences.reason: Each of these lines is `exactType(Component, defineComponent({...}))`: the upstream helper compares the two types for identity, so it only accepts a default export that is the very type vue-tsc generates for the SFC. Vize types the default export as its own component contract (`__vizeCheck`, `__vizeRawProps`, `__vizeEmitProps`, `__vizeFallthroughProps`, ... intersected with the public constructor), and every consumer-side check reads that contract off `typeof Component`: generic prop resolution, raw props, emit listeners, fallthrough props and structural slots. The contract is what makes those checks exact for components that reach a template through a barrel, a registration or a value, which an identical-to-vue-tsc export cannot carry. The components behave identically in every other project of the corpus (their props, emits, slots, models and exposed instances are checked there); only their identity with `defineComponent` differs. Closing this needs the contract to move off the default export, which is tracked separately.
